author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page value below 1 as the first page
summary: Opening the owner listing with any page value below 1 shows the normal listing of the first page instead of the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a page value below 1, however far below (zero, a negative value, a value too far below 1 for the system to hold as a number), when the owner listing is requested, then the first page of owners is listed with HTTP 200 rather than the error page
given a page value below 1, when the owner listing is shown, then the first page is presented as the current page

given a page value below 1 and a last name, when the search runs, then the outcome matches the same search on the first page: a single match opens that owner's record, several matches are listed, no match reports that no owner was found
non_goals: The veterinarian directory: the request names the owner listing only; recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md
Page values of 1 or above, including values past the last page: the request covers values below 1 only
Non-numeric page values: the request covers values below 1 only
notes: Intake line 1 quotes the request and records no decisions. The request contradicts no requirement or Non-Goals row, so no consultation was raised. The request asks that the cause be found; the design and implementation stages own naming it. The audit found no prd-autofix records. docs/prd.md delta: REQ-OWN-005 narrative, anchor, three Done-when bullets, and one open question.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: OwnerController (docs/system-design.md § Contracts, new 'Owner listing page value' note) keeps the slice; architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog *Web controller* row names range normalization as binding, so the clamp is no business rule and no service or ADR is needed. There are two causes, both at the handler. (1) page=0 or a negative value reaches PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...), which rejects a negative index and raises IllegalArgumentException, hence the 500 error page. (2) A value below the int range never reaches the handler: `int page` fails type conversion and yields the 400 error page, so a clamp on `int` cannot satisfy the first acceptance criterion. Adjustment: bind page as java.math.BigInteger, keeping defaultValue "1", and normalize once at the head of processFindForm into one int that feeds both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel. No oracle connected; basis is grep and read of OwnerController.java:95-137 and VetController.java:45-61, the weaker basis.
integration_points: Binding: GET /owners is an existing entry point; page stays a request-scoped scalar parameter, now BigInteger. Owner binding and its disallowed fields are unchanged.
Double, framework transport: MockMvc, per testing-principles § mocking policy.

Double, repository: the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository in OwnerControllerTests, the suite's current stub; no real double is required for this web-level rule. Because the stubs match any(Pageable.class), the listing test must also capture or match the Pageable and assert page index 0, otherwise a broken query passes.
Test level: web level only, per testing-principles line 64 (a rule assigned to the web controller is tested there); do not extract it for a unit test.

patterns.description: Handler to change. Spring's String-to-Number conversion covers BigInteger, so non-numeric input fails conversion exactly as it does for int.
Equivalence classes for the page value: zero, negative, and a value beyond long range, as rows of one table-driven test where outcomes share a kind.

risks.risk: PRD non-goal: a clamp alone does not preserve behaviour above the range. A value above int range is a 400 error page today (system-design § Owner listing page value), and BigInteger would let it through or, via intValueExact, turn it into a 500.
risks.mitigation: After the below-1 clamp, reject a value above Integer.MAX_VALUE with ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST) with a fixed reason. Pin with tests: above-int range and non-numeric each stay status 400. These are extra regression tests beyond the prd-entry's test_names.

risks.risk: Integer.MIN_VALUE trap: arithmetic on the raw value before comparison can overflow. A narrowing such as BigInteger.intValue() on a far-below value wraps to an arbitrary int (system-design § Owner listing page value).
risks.mitigation: Compare as BigInteger first; narrow only after the range is known. Include a value below Long.MIN_VALUE and Integer.MIN_VALUE itself in the table.

risks.risk: Normalizing only the query leaves currentPage at the raw value, so the second acceptance criterion fails and the pagination template renders wrong links.
risks.mitigation: The one normalized int is the only value after the handler head; the test asserts model attribute currentPage equals 1.

risks.risk: Owner listing and last-name search path, row 'Owner listing and last-name search' in system-design § Scale and Load.
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form; the path stays one fixed-size page per request.

risks.risk: Page value parsing scales with parameter length, row 'Owner listing page value' in system-design § Scale and Load.
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: framework conversion, one comparison; length is capped by the container's request-line limit. The error reason must not echo the value (security-principles § secret disclosure through logs and errors applies to the rendered message).

risks.risk: Scope drift into VetController, which has the same defect, or into values past the last page.
risks.mitigation: Leave both unchanged; prd-entry non_goals and the PRD's open question hold them. No shared helper with the vet package: the packages do not reference each other (system-design § Package Structure).

notes: Verdict is minor: the design delta is the wider binding type and the normalization note, plus a § Scale and Load section the design doc lacked (doctor template, doc-sync maintenance); it carries two rows marked derived and unconfirmed. Design-doc writes: Contracts row for OwnerController, the page-value note, § Scale and Load. No ADR: the choice is contained in one slice. No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Five-signal check: no signal trips.

author: change-grader
summary: normalize owner listing page values below 1 to the first page

blast_radius.note: Production reach is one handler plus one private helper in OwnerController. No sensitive paths, and most of the 21 hunks are imports, test code and docs. The vet directory and templates are untouched, and no production or test caller depends on the old int signature.

semantic_surprise.note: Read toCurrentPage: the upper guard runs first, then the clamp, then the narrowing, so intValue() is always in 1..Integer.MAX_VALUE and both the query and currentPage use that one int. Above-int values stay 400 through a new explicit path with a fixed reason. No live request was exercised, but nothing in the diff behaves beyond its description.

test_adequacy.note: Most tests are real: only Franklin is stubbed in setup, so the firstPage() matcher fails on a wrong page index. But the far-below rows do not pin the narrowing trap the design named. BELOW_LONG_RANGE_PAGE narrows to -1, so a broken Math.max(page.intValue(), 1) passes all four rows, while a value like -4294967291 would land on page 5.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four approved in round one with no findings, and the security citations and greps I checked resolve. Caveats remain: security states the Tomcat size limit it relies on was not read and that its test run was up-to-date with no live request. The test reviewer lists the below-long boundary as covered, which overstates that row.

scope_deviation.note: No retries, consultations or design revisions, and the vet directory and past-last-page values stay out. The above-int guard preserves existing 400 behavior and the design-block places it. The new Scale and Load section goes beyond the bug but is recorded in the design-block and marked derived and unconfirmed.

rationale: The fix reads correct, and the production change is small. The residual risk is one surviving mutant: no test row catches narrowing before clamping. Read toCurrentPage, consider adding a row such as -4294967291, and confirm the container-limit claim now in system-design.
